source.authors: Dylan G.E. Gomes, Holger R. Goerlitz
source.title: Individual differences show that only some bats can cope with noise-induced masking and distraction

method: behavioural: two-alternative forced choice, flat reference disc versus rippled discs (seven ripple heights) by echolocation, tested in silence and under three band-limited noise treatments; separate GLM per bat with Bonferroni correction
conditions: Captive colony at the Max Planck Institute for Ornithology, Seewiesen; nine bats trained, four (three males, one female) reached criterion and were tested; 30 trials per ripple height and noise combination per bat (990 trials per bat). Noise: smooth non-overlapping (5-35 kHz), smooth-overlapping (40-90 kHz), sparse-overlapping (40-90 kHz with random silent gaps). Per tool summary of Results (not quoted): noise did not change discrimination performance of bats A and B; performance decreased for bats C and D under smooth-overlapping noise (z = -3.2, p = 0.008; z = -3.2, p = 0.004); all four bats raised call sound pressure level by about 10-13 dB in overlapping noise. Sample is four trained individuals, so no population rate is implied.
quote: Additionally, we highlight that only some individuals were able to cope with noise, while others were not.

source.authors: Samuel A. Shively-Moore, B. G. Chethana Chathuprabha, Patrick A. Guerra, Stephen F. Matter
source.title: Summer Eastern North American Monarchs Do Not Use Magnetic Field for Directionality but Extreme Heat Alters Righting Behavior

method: behavioural: righting-response orientation assay inside a Helmholtz coil system, three trials per animal (pre-treatment, treatment, post-treatment); orientation tested against the 0 degree null with V-test and Rayleigh test, plus a Bayesian circular mixed-effects model
conditions: Wild adult summer monarchs of both sexes collected on the wing, 24 June to 1 September 2025, at the University of Cincinnati Center for Field Studies, Harrison, Ohio. The coils were used to keep the field consistent with the local geomagnetic field (Methods sentence read in two pieces), so the study did not rotate or otherwise alter magnetic direction (tool summary). Groups by temperature treatment: control (28 C light, 20 C dark), long-term heat (35 C light, 20 C dark after two days of acclimation), short-term heat (heat during the trial only). Per tool summary of the Results (not quoted): completed trials per group were control 14, 13, 12; long-term 27, 5, 12; short-term 5, 2, 2 (pre, during, post), because not all animals finished every trial; every group's mean orientation did not differ from 0 degrees (control pre-treatment mu = 359, r = 0.965, Rayleigh Z = 13.043, p < 0.001); the Bayesian model found no difference among treatments or trials; long-term heat reduced righting completion (Fisher exact, pre vs post p = 0.009), short-term heat had no significant effect (p = 0.273). Null result of a righting assay in an unaltered field, so it does not exclude magnetoreception tested by other designs.
quote: We found that summer monarchs would right themselves, but did not use a magnetic compass to orient northward.

source.title: The effect of underwater sounds on shark behaviour

method: behavioural: field playback from a speaker mounted between the cameras of a baited, downward-facing midwater stereo-video rig; treatments orca call sequence, an artificially generated sound with 95% of its energy below 1 kHz, and a silent control with a non-functional speaker
conditions: Free-swimming wild white sharks at Mossel Bay, South Africa (Hartenbos and Seal Island sites), attracted with chum; 101 deployments (44 control, 24 orca, 33 artificial sound) and 593 interactions with 38 individually identified sharks (tool summary of the Results). Per tool summary (not quoted), white-shark nulls for both sounds: presence (orca p = 0.19, artificial p = 0.51), interactions (orca p = 0.27, artificial p = 0.72), behavioural score (orca p = 0.69, artificial p = 0.72); reduced time on screen with the artificial sound, though the p values printed for time on screen looked inconsistent with the text; experienced sharks spent less time with the artificial sound (p = 0.05) and showed no difference for orca (p = 0.79). Reef and coastal sharks at Exmouth, Western Australia (seven species) did reduce approaches with both sounds and are not part of this record. Speaker output was an in-water playback, so level at the animal is not a measured threshold; the study shows reaction to sound, not an audiogram.
quote: White sharks spent less time around the baited camera rig when the artificial sound was presented, but showed no significant difference in behaviour in response to orca calls.

source.authors: C. Elisa Schaum, Robert Batty, Kim S. Last
source.title: Smelling Danger – Alarm Cue Responses in the Polychaete Nereis (Hediste) diversicolor (Müller, 1776) to Potential Fish Predation

method: behavioural bioassay: night-time emergences from artificial burrows under infrared CCTV with motion-capture software, flounder-conditioned seawater and flounder mucous in seawater, seawater control
conditions: Wild harbour ragworms collected August and September 2008 from the Loch Gilp shore, Scotland, with juvenile flounder and plaice, and held in stock tanks (Methods sentence read in two pieces). Worms kept in four aquaria with eight artificial burrows each, filmed night-time by infrared CCTV and scored by motion software for number of emergences, emergence duration and distance from burrow entrance; worms in a tank pooled as non-independent. Per tool summary of the paper (not read as whole sentences): bioassay 1 used flounder-conditioned seawater from 6 down to 2 fish (n = 32 worms, 16 per treatment, seven nights) with no significant reduction at 4 fish or fewer (emergence number F6,29 = 1.1, p > 0.1) and a significant reduction at 5 or more fish; bioassay 2 used flounder mucous at eight concentrations 0.1 to 1.2 ug/ml (N = 16 per treatment, three nights) with no significant reduction at 0.2 ug/ml or less (emergence number F7,34 = 2.3, p > 0.1) and a significant reduction at 0.4 ug/ml and above; plaice and herring mucous gave similar responses (F2,388 = 0.48, p > 0.5); the series sit between tested steps, so 0.4 ug/ml is the lowest concentration that reduced emergence in this series, not a measured detection threshold.
quote: Using CCTV and motion capture software, we show that H. diversicolor is able to detect chemical cues associated with the presence of juvenile flounder (Platichthys flesus).
note: Whole abstract sentence of 26 words, read intact in two abutting pieces (end reached).
